title: Mixed scalar/site normalization for direct-image/open pastes
statement:
Use Grothendieck topoi with fixed small-site presentations [def-weil-pbc-topos] and constant sheaves of commutative rings. A morphism of topoi $v:T\to W$ means an adjunction $v^{-1}\dashv v_*$ with $v^{-1}$ preserving finite limits. For a ring $R$, write $D_R(T)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $L_{v,R}=v^{-1}$ and $R_{v,R}=Rv_*$, with their derived adjunction and counit $\varepsilon_{v,R}$. An open embedding means the inclusion of the slice topos of a subterminal object; its exact extension by zero $I_{j,R}$ is left adjoint to $L_{j,R}$, fully faithful, with unit $\eta_{j,R}:1\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{j,R}I_{j,R}$. All equations below insert the canonical inverse-image and direct-image compositors. For a unital ring map $A\to B$ put $S_T=-\otimes_A^LB$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and let $U_T:D_B(T)\to D_A(T)$ be exact restriction of scalars. Use the canonical tensor/pullback comparison $\lambda_v:L_{v,B}S_W\xrightarrow{\sim}S_TL_{v,A}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Define $\chi_v:S_WR_{v,A}\to R_{v,B}S_T$ as the adjoint transpose of $S_T(\varepsilon_{v,A})\lambda_v$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], and, for an open embedding $j:V\hookrightarrow T$, $\beta_j:S_TI_{j,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}I_{j,B}S_V$ as the balancing map induced by tensoring sections on the open and the zero map on its complement. Let $A\to B$ now be finite free. For $W=X,T,Y$ let $\widetilde W$ be another such topos with comparison morphism $\nu_W:\widetilde W\to W$, and write $N_{W,R}=\nu_W^{-1}$. Let $X\xrightarrow jT\xrightarrow pY$ and $\widetilde X\xrightarrow{\widetilde j}\widetilde T\xrightarrow{\widetilde p}\widetilde Y$ be commuting diagrams, with $j,\widetilde j$ open embeddings, and assume the open square is Cartesian: $\widetilde X$ is the open subtopos of $\widetilde T$ cut out by the image under $\nu_T^{-1}$ of the subterminal object defining $X$, $\widetilde j$ is its inclusion and $\nu_X$ the induced morphism. Specify the commutation of inverse images by their canonical composition identifications. Write $F_R=R_{p,R}I_{j,R}$ and $\widetilde F_R=R_{\widetilde p,R}I_{\widetilde j,R}$, and use the counit-transpose coefficient maps $c=c_{p,j}$ and $\widetilde c=c_{\widetilde p,\widetilde j}$ defined by the displayed constituents above (the subscript $R$ on $F$ denotes its coefficient ring).
Let $d_{p,R}:N_{Y,R}R_{p,R}\to R_{\widetilde p,R}N_{T,R}$ be the mate of the inverse-image identification, normalized by the direct-image counit. Assume $d_{p,R}$ is invertible on the displayed inputs. Let $e_{j,R}:N_{T,R}I_{j,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}I_{\widetilde j,R}N_{X,R}$ be the inverse of the $I_{\widetilde j,R}\dashv L_{\widetilde j,R}$ adjunct $I_{\widetilde j,R}N_{X,R}\to N_{T,R}I_{j,R}$ of $N_{X,R}(\eta_{j,R})$ (after $L_{\widetilde j,R}N_{T,R}\cong N_{X,R}L_{j,R}$); by the Cartesian hypothesis this adjunct is invertible, so $e$ is normalized by the open unit. Set
$$C_{p,j,R}=R_{\widetilde p,R}(e_{j,R})\,d_{p,R,I_{j,R}(-)}:N_{Y,R}F_R\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde F_RN_{X,R},$$
and let $\delta_W:S_{\widetilde W}N_{W,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}N_{W,B}S_W$ be the canonical scalar/pullback comparison. The inverse-image identifications and $\delta$ are those induced on tensors by pulling back a section and its coefficient, with the usual insertion-of-one inverse; no independent choice of mates is made. Then the following equality holds in $D_B(\widetilde Y)$:
$$\widetilde F_B(\delta_X)\,\widetilde c_{N_{X,A}M}\,S_{\widetilde Y}(C_{p,j,A,M})
=C_{p,j,B,S_XM}\,N_{Y,B}(c_{p,j,M})\,\delta_{Y,F_AM}.$$
It is natural in $M$. The coefficient map on the tilde side is the actual scalar-adjunction transpose defined from restriction of scalars for $\widetilde F$, as well as the proper-counit/open-balancing composite. Thus this identity compares the specified constructions, not merely isomorphic objects.

The identity applies simultaneously to finite diagrams of these factorizations. Suppose a comparison between their composite functors is a finite paste of direct-image compositors, open-extension compositors, and open-adjunction mates of invertible restriction exchanges. Assume all the needed $d$ and exchange maps are invertible on the inputs, and identify the corresponding comparisons on the two systems by their counit and open-unit normalizations. For a word $H$ in the direct-image and open-extension functors, write $c_H$ for its coefficient comparison obtained by pasting the $\chi$ and $\beta$, and $C_{H,R}$ for its site comparison obtained by pasting $d$ and $e$. For such a pasted natural transformation $\theta_R:H_R\to H'_R$, its normalized site square is
$$C_{H',R}\,N_Y(\theta_R)=\widetilde\theta_R N_X\,C_{H,R}.$$
Its scalar square is
$$c_{H'}\,S_Y(\theta_A)=\theta_B S_X\,c_H.$$
The normalized site squares hold for the indicated generators and their finite pastes. Whenever the scalar square holds on the untilde system, it holds for $\widetilde\theta$ on all inputs $N_{X,A}M$ on the tilde system. The assertion includes inverses of invertible comparisons and proper-refinement comparisons $r:F^{c'}\xrightarrow{\sim}F^c$. In particular, a coefficient/refinement identity $c^c S(r_A)=r_B c^{c'}$ or a coefficient/composition identity $c_{gf}S(\alpha_A)=\alpha_B F_{g,B}(c_f)c_{g,F_{f,A}(-)}$ on the untilde system gives the corresponding identity on the tilde system. These equations persist under conjugation by natural input isomorphisms $N_{X,A}M\cong K$, and are independent of the chosen such presentation through its canonical conjugation. No faithfulness of restriction of scalars or of comparison pullback on derived morphisms is assumed.

proof.text: The Lean proof checks the ordinary restriction cube first. Apply the faithful underlying-set-sheaf functor on ordinary A-module sheaves and postcompose with the two invertible underlying inverse-image identifications at the target. On the right use the target scalar/site restriction normalization, naturality of its A inverse-image identification, scalar restriction normalization for p, and the normalized A site square. On the left use the normalized B site square, tilde scalar restriction normalization, naturality of the tilde A inverse-image identification, and the source scalar/site restriction normalization. Both give the identical set-square composite. No derived functor is asserted faithful. The six exact functor squares descend as a cube by mapDerivedCategory_exactCube. Take scalar-adjunction mates of the two equal derived pastes; mateEquiv_vcomp and the two whiskering identities identify them using exactly each ScalarPullback.mate_normalized field. Cancel the mapped A site isomorphism to obtain the inverse scalar cube, then conjugate by the invertible scalar comparisons to obtain the required forward cube. This argument does not use finite freeness; the supplied scalar adjunction and normalized comparison data suffice.

proof.text:
Take mates of the two equal pastes of Step 1 along the geometric adjunctions. Clause (1) of the mate-pasting lemma identifies each pasted mate with the paste of its mates. The mates of $\lambda_p$ and $\lambda_{\widetilde p}$ are precisely $\chi_p$ and $\chi_{\widetilde p}$, and the mates of $a_A,a_B$ are the specified $d_{p,A},d_{p,B}$. Consequently, for every $K\in D_A(T)$,
$$R_{\widetilde p,B}(\delta_{T,K})\,\chi_{\widetilde p,N_{T,A}K}\,S_{\widetilde Y}(d_{p,A,K})
=d_{p,B,S_TK}\,N_{Y,B}(\chi_{p,K})\,\delta_{Y,R_{p,A}K}.$$
This identifies the actual counit-defined arrows: the mate bijection characterizes each arrow by its counit transpose. No invertibility of $d$ or $\chi$ is used in this step. In Lean direct_mixed applies exchangeMate_cube to the scalar cube of Step 1, with the two site inverse-image isomorphisms in inverse direction. Its conclusion is conjugated by the source and target scalar/site isomorphisms. This calculation does not require either direct site comparison to be invertible.

proof.text: For the open constituent, apply the same abstract scalar mate cube to the four open adjunctions, the isomorphisms beta, e_B, e_A and tildeBeta, and the two scalar/site comparisons in inverse direction. The restriction cube required for this application is the inverse scalar cube of Step 1 for j, conjugated by the two inverse-image site isomorphisms. The four mate-normalization fields of OpenSquare identify its faces. Conjugate the resulting equation by the invertible open scalar/site composites. This gives precisely the MixedAt equation for openValue. Only invertibility of the supplied open comparison isomorphisms is used; no inverse of a direct-image coefficient comparison is taken.

proof.text:
Expand $C_A=R_{\widetilde p,A}(e_A)d_A$ and $\widetilde c=R_{\widetilde p,B}(\beta_{\widetilde j})\chi_{\widetilde p}$. In the left side of the required equation, naturality of $\chi_{\widetilde p}$ moves $S_{\widetilde Y}R_{\widetilde p,A}(e_A)$ across $\chi_{\widetilde p}$. The three resulting factors inside $R_{\widetilde p,B}$ are the left side of Step 3. Replace them by its right side. The remaining adjacent factors are exactly the left side of Step 2 at $K=I_{j,A}M$. Replace those by its right side. Finally naturality of $d_{p,B}$ at $\beta_j$ gives
$$R_{\widetilde p,B}(e_{j,B})\,d_{p,B,I_{j,B}S_XM}\,N_{Y,B}\bigl(R_{p,B}(\beta_j)\chi_{p,I_{j,A}M}\bigr)\,\delta_{Y,F_AM},$$
which is $C_{p,j,B,S_XM}N_{Y,B}(c_{p,j,M})\delta_{Y,F_AM}$. This proves the displayed mixed square. Each manipulation is naturality or functoriality applied to the preceding two proved equations. In Lean the displayed factorization identity is obtained by specializing word_mixed (Step 6) to the two-letter word consisting of the open extension followed by the direct image. The open letter has no additional invertibility condition; the direct letter has exactly the two displayed assumptions. The word comparisons unfold definitionally to the factorization comparisons. This specialization does not use the factorization theorem in the proof of word_mixed.

proof.text: Apply the finite-free constituent lemma separately to $(p,j)$ and $(\widetilde p,\widetilde j)$. It says not only that the displayed $c$ is invertible, but that its scalar-adjunction transpose is $\rho\circ F_A(\eta^S)$, with the section-normalized restriction comparison $\rho$. For the tilde system this is precisely the scalar-adjunction construction required in the statement. Therefore the tilde arrow used in Step 4 is the specified restriction-of-scalars transpose, as well as the counit/balancing composite. This application needs only a finite free unital ring map and the topoi and open embeddings already assumed; it imposes no properness or boundedness condition.

proof.text:
Extend the mixed square to a word $H$ by induction on its length. Use identities for the empty word. For one letter the result is Step 2 or Step 3. For a concatenation $GK$ the definitions read $c_{GK}=G_B(c_K)c_GK_A$ and $C_{GK,R}=\widetilde G_R(C_{K,R})C_{G,R}K_R$. Expand both expressions, move the middle comparison past the next one by naturality, and substitute first the equation for $G$ and then that for $K$. This yields
$$\widetilde H_B(\delta_X)\,\widetilde c_HN_{X,A}\,S_{\widetilde Y}(C_{H,A})=C_{H,B}S_X\,N_{Y,B}(c_H)\,\delta_YH_A.$$
The induction uses the one-letter equations on the indicated intermediate inputs, so the inputwise invertibility assumptions apply exactly where needed. It does not require that $N$ be essentially surjective. The Lean proof separates mixed compatibility from invertibility. First, induction proves MixedAt for every word, without site invertibility assumptions. The concatenation calculation moves the inner A-site comparison through the outer tilde coefficient comparison by naturality, applies the inner and outer mixed identities, then uses naturality of the outer B-site comparison. A second induction proves invertibility at arbitrary independent A and B input objects from SiteInvertibleAt. This generality is necessary because a concatenation sends the B input through the preceding B functor; it is not definitionally the scalar extension of the intermediate A input. Combining the two inductions gives word_mixed.

proof.text: Check normalized site squares for compositors. For composable direct images, their compositors are conjugates of the inverse-image composition identifications. Clause (2) of mate pasting identifies the mate of the composite inverse-image square with the composite of the two $d$'s. Thus the site square for the direct-image compositor commutes. For composable opens, take left mates of the inverse restriction-composition square: the open compositor has transpose the composite of its two open units. The inverse of the resulting mate is exactly the paste of the two $e$'s, since each $e^{-1}$ is normalized by that same unit. This proves the site square for the open compositor. For identities, clause (4) gives the identity mate. These are statements about the named compositors with the canonical associators, not chosen isomorphisms of their endpoints.

proof.text: For a restriction exchange, apply the exchange-mate cube lemma with the four geometric inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions, the four comparison pullbacks $N$, and the canonical comparison squares of inverse images. Its inverse-image-cube hypothesis is associativity of the specified pullback identifications. Its conclusion is exactly the site square for the counit-defined restriction exchange. If that exchange is invertible on the specified input, multiply this square by its inverse on both sides; this gives the square for the inverse exchange. Next take the open adjunct: the mate bijection and the changing-adjunction clauses (3a),(3b) of mate pasting carry that square to the square for its open-adjunction mate, because the comparison of open adjoints is $e^{-1}$, whose unit transpose is fixed in the item. This checks the remaining generator, including the prescribed unit and counit normalizations. Only the inverses stipulated in the item are taken. In particular this argument applies to any proper-refinement comparison represented by the assumed finite paste, without asserting that an arbitrary refinement square is Cartesian.

proof.text: The site-square equation is preserved by finite pasting. For a vertical composite $\psi\theta$, substitute the site square for $\theta$, then the one for $\psi$; the middle comparison cancels. For a horizontal composite, whisker the two site squares and use naturality to interchange the middle arrows. The same multiplication by inverses proves the assertion for inverses of invertible comparisons. Induction on the finite paste, starting with Steps 7 and 8, proves the asserted site square for every $\theta$ in the statement. All intermediate inverses of $C$ exist on the indicated inputs because they are pastes of the assumed invertible $d$ and $e$.

proof.text: For transfer_scalar_square obtain the two mixed identities and the A-site isomorphism from word_mixed. Precompose the proposed tilde scalar square with S_tildeY(C_H,A,M), which is invertible, and postcompose it with Hprime_tildeB(delta_X,M), which is also invertible. The A-site square moves theta_tildeA to N_Y,A(theta_A) followed by C_Hprime,A. Substitute the mixed identity for Hprime. Naturality of delta_Y moves theta_A past delta_Y, and functoriality groups S_Y(theta_A) followed by c_Hprime. Replace this composite using the untilde scalar-square hypothesis. The B-site square moves theta_B past C_Hprime,B. Substitute the mixed identity for H in the reverse direction, then use naturality of theta_tildeB at delta_X. The resulting equality is the other side of the precomposed and postcomposed tilde square. Cancel the two isomorphisms. No faithfulness is used, and no inverse to a coefficient map is required. For paste_transfer, obtain the site-square hypothesis by paste_site from the given PasteAt derivation, and apply transfer_scalar_square. Taking theta to be the specified refinement or composition comparison gives the corresponding assertions in the statement.

proof.text: Form natural transformations a = S_tildeY(theta_tildeA) followed by c_Hprime and b = c_H followed by theta_tildeB(S_tildeX), between the same two composite functors. The assertion TildeScalarAt(K) is a.app K = b.app K. For an input isomorphism i : K -> Kprime, precompose the equality at Kprime by the image of i under the common source functor. Naturality of a and b reduces the equation to the equality at K postcomposed by the image of i under the common target functor. The source image of i is invertible, so cancellation proves the forward implication. Apply the same argument to i inverse for the reverse implication. Applying this equivalence to the canonical composite of two input presentations proves independence under that conjugation. This is a naturality argument in the derived categories and makes no faithfulness assumption.

proof_origin.place: Steps 1 and 3: M8 stage-3 formalization. Ordinary restriction normalization and faithfulness prove the cube before localization; exact-cube descent and scalar mates give the scalar cube. Geometric mates and open mates give the two constituent mixed equations, and naturality gives the word equation. The factorization equation is its two-letter specialization. Scalar-square cancellation, input conjugation and paste-to-transfer application are complete Lean proofs. The original tilde-transpose theorem (Step 5) and normalized generator site-square theorem (Steps 7-9) remain sorry with their original statements and proof docstrings.
